item.title: The first 21 chapters of Quarterback of the Future are available
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: For the 25th anniversary of the launch of PFT, I decided to post the rewritten Quarterback of the Future — one chapter per day.
item.content:encoded:
For the 25th anniversary of the launch of PFT, I decided to post the rewritten Quarterback of the Future — one chapter per day.

Three weeks in, 21 chapters are available. The full menu is here, with a button at the bottom of each chapter to quickly move to the next.

The chapters are short. Which means there are plenty of them. But each one reads quickly and, ideally, tempts the reader to read the next one.

It's the writer's job to make the reader want to do that. If you haven't started, here’s Chapter One. If you like it, click to Chapter Two.

I may accelerate the process as we get into the holiday season, possibly increasing to two or three per day.

If you want to wait until more are posted, that's fine. All chapters will remain up until all of them are posted. After that, we'll leave it up for a while, if you want to be able to read the whole thing without getting to the end of what's been released and don't want to wait.

The whole thing is a thank you to those of you who have been out there since the early days, when we didn't know what we were doing and it looked like it.

Actually, not much has changed.

item.title: Jerry Jones on fan's death after fight at 49ers-Cowboys game: "We had no record of an incident"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: This week, a fan died after falling during a fight at AT&T Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
This week, a fan died after falling during a fight at AT&T Stadium. The fan was there to watch the 49ers-Cowboys game.

On Friday, Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones was asked about the incident during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan.

"I just got that information, and so we had no record of of an incident, and we'll be obviously looking into that," Jones said. "My understanding is that the individual went to the game and didn't feel good at the game, and then left, and [had] been hospitalized. But we weren't aware of any incident that involved a fan at the game."

They know about it now, and they have the resources to fully investigate.

"We really do have quite a — eons above what it was 10, 15 years ago," Jones said. "We have quite a surveillance of what's going on at every aspect of our game. And so it is really rare if we didn't know of any incident. We've got too many people out there. We have 6,000 workers on game day."

Jones said he'll pass along any surveillance footage the Cowboys have to investigators.

A full and complete investigation could potentially create liability for the venue. It all depends on the facts. And, frankly, it requires the authorities not to sit and wait for whatever is voluntarily provided but to use the subpoena power to go get anything and everything that will allow the complicated puzzle to be put together as to what happened to Marco Narro, whether it could have or should been prevented, and whether the aftermath could have or should have been handled differently.

item.title: Tom Brady, after selling Birmingham City stake, buys piece of Chelsea
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Tom Brady's exit from the English soccer business was only temporary.
item.content:encoded:
Tom Brady's exit from the English soccer business was only temporary.

After selling his stake in Birmingham City, Brady has reportedly purchased a slice of the Chelsea soccer club, albeit indirectly.

Via ESPN, Brady will become a minority investor in Clearlake Capital, the entity that controls Chelsea.

Separate reporting from the Times characterizes the situation as Brady being "in talks" to take a "small minority stake" within the portion of Clearlake Capital that owns Chelsea. Brady, per the Times, also would become a member of the board of advisors.

Whether that means he'll eventually be criticizing the work ethic of the team's manager remains to be seen.

The end result is that Brady hasn't streamlined his overall portfolio in an effort to achieve more "balance" in his life. Instead, he's swapping out his piece of a second-tier club for interest in a member of the Premier League.

item.title: Daiyan Henley being out with a knee injury changes nothing about the failed trade to Broncos
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The failed trade of Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley returned to the front burner on Friday, with the news that Henley will miss Sunday's game against the Jets due to a knee injury.
item.content:encoded:
The failed trade of Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley returned to the front burner on Friday, with the news that Henley will miss Sunday's game against the Jets due to a knee injury.

It was a knee condition that prompted the Broncos to pull the plug on the deal — after trying to renegotiate the terms after the trade deadline.

From Mike Klis of 9News, who covers the Broncos: "Chargers ILB Daiyan Henley missed entire week of practices with knee injury and has been ruled out for game vs Jets. This validates concerns raised by Broncos medical team and GM George Paton. And proves Chargers were not on the up and up."

Does it really prove that the Chargers weren't "on the up and up"? The issue is that the Denver physical flagged a knee problem. In lieu of finding that the physical had been failed and that the trade won't happen, the Broncos were willing to give Henley a passing grade, if the compensation was changed.

Henley has played every game this season. He played on Monday night against the Ravens. As far as anyone knows, he injured the knee during that game.

As far as anyone knows, the currently injured knee isn't the same knee that created the concern during the Denver physical.

It's all just noise at this point. The core problem is the ability of a team — after the trade deadline has passed — to renegotiate the terms of a trade. And the related issue is the ability of a team to give a conditional grade on the pass-fail question of a physical that is tied to the specific compensation.

A player either passes the physical, or he fails it. The process shouldn't include an epilogue premised on the outcome of the physical being "maybe." Especially after the time for negotiating trades has ended.

item.title: Raiders owner Mark Davis hated the Madden movie
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Did anyone read the script before allowing the Raiders' name and logo to be used?
item.content:encoded:
The new Madden movie includes a brief, fleeting glance of a young Mark Davis. The depiction wasn't flattering.

His assessment of the film is far less flattering.

The Raiders owner teed off on the Madden movie, in an interview with John Katsolimetes of the Las Vegas Review-Journal.

“My comment is, it’s full of turducken," Davis said initially.

Is that a good thing or a bad thing?

“It depends on whether you like turducken or not, and obviously, I don’t like turducken," Davis said.

His biggest concern was the script.

“I think it’s really it’s unfair to take people that have passed away and make caricatures out of them, and try to sell it as truth,” Davis said. “They start the movie with a statement saying that all of it’s not true, but some of it is, so it’s confusing what to believe.”

That's not an uncommon device. "Based on a true story" means that plenty of liberties will be taken in an effort to make the story more compelling.

Mark Davis had one specific concern regarding the shading of the truth. He objected to his father's reaction to the serious neck injury suffered by Patriots receiver Darryl Stingley, during a preseason game in 1978.

“So John goes over to the hospital afterwards, you know, and really looks after him," Mark Davis said, "and there’s a scene where my dad is telling John, ‘You don’t need to go over there. You don’t need to take care of other teams’ players. You take care of our players.'

"That’s just so far from the truth. Anybody who has ever known him knows my dad always took care of people behind the scenes. If it was a player from another team had an issue that wasn’t being taken care of, my dad would quietly take care of that even if it was players on other teams. I’m serious. . . . It just it felt cheap to me to build up John’s image at the expense of my father’s.”

Davis praised Christian Bale for his portrayal of Al Davis.

“You can’t blame the script on him," Mark Davis said. "He tried.”

Mark Davis also didn't care for the characterization of the iconic John Madden by Nicolas Cage.

“You know, he at times did look like John, but he wasn’t John," Davis said. "I mean, they made John to be a pussy, and John was the farthest thing from a pussy.”

The end result could be a positive. Mark Davis is now motivated to create something that properly and accurately depicts his father.

“I don’t know what this movie’s purpose was, to be honest," Mark Davis said. "But you know, it’s making me more and more realize that I’m going to have to put together something on my dad. It could be a movie, it could be a characterization, but at least it’ll be truthful. . . .

“I think I need to do that, or at least let people know that I’m thinking about doing that, so that don’t jump in and think that they can do it first.”

The concerns expressed by Mark Davis regarding the script raise the question of whether he or the league or anyone bothered to review it before allowing the producers to use the Raiders name, colors, and logos in the filming of the football sequences. That's a critical aspect when it comes to the overall credibility of a film about pro football.

If it looks real, it feels real. Unlike other films that didn't secure the ability to use actual team names and logos (Any Given Sunday, The Replacements).

And that's the irony of this. Davis and the league allowed the Raiders name and uniforms to be included in the film, giving it the impression of accuracy and authenticity. Which, in turn, makes the story seem accurate and authentic. Which makes it even harder to separate the truth from the fiction.

Here's hoping Mark Davis comes up with a way to tell the true story of Al Davis. With no embellishment, fabrication, or Hollywood tricks aimed at making the story seem better than it was.

Because the story of Al Davis would be pretty damn compelling if it were indeed confined to the strict parameters of reality.

item.title: NFL didn't know Puka Nacua had surgery when agreeing to suspension
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The sudden decision of the NFL to suspend receiver Puka Nacua three games raises plenty of relevant questions.
item.content:encoded:
The sudden decision of the NFL to suspend receiver Puka Nacua three games raises plenty of relevant questions. On Friday, a technically irrelevant question was answered.

After Rams coach Sean McVay disclosed to reporters that Nacua had surgery to repair a torn MCL suffered during a Week 9 win over the Commanders, Judy Battista of NFL Network reported this: "The NFL did not know Puka Nacua had had knee surgery on Tuesday when it suspended him yesterday."

Surely, that's accurate; Judy is a solid reporter. But that extra fact doesn't matter to the NFL's ultimate handling of Nacua.

The report creates the impression that, during the negotiations that resulted in the three-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy, Nacua and/or his representatives withheld material information. That, at some level, the league had been duped by the lack of knowledge that Nacua had undergone surgery that will sideline him for "a couple months."

First, the suspension (as the league affirmatively explained on Thursday) is separate from the injury. The NFL listed multiple examples of players who served suspensions while injured.

Second, whether Nacua (who had already missed one of the four minimum games he's required to miss while on IR), was already going to serve the entirety of the suspension while on injured reserve with or without surgery.

Third, the surgery and the extended absence actually avoids the possibility that Nacua would have returned to action exactly one game after finishing his suspension, resulting in no net games missed due to the suspension.

The mere existence of the report represents an implicit acknowledgement by the league that the negotiated suspension, aimed at allowing Nacua to double-dip when it comes to his stint on injured reserve and his suspension, underscores the broader question of whether players should be allowed to serve a suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy when otherwise unable to play. That's a separate issue for the NFL to revisit, if it chooses, through a potential revision to the terms of the policy.

As explained on Friday, the league could have refused the deal. It could have insisted on pushing the issue through the full process, with Judge Sue L. Robinson conducting a hearing and the outcome potentially being appealed (by Nacua and/or the league) to the Commissioner. But that would have entailed a non-zero-percent chance that Nacua wouldn't have been suspended at all.

For Nacua, the goal was to get the suspension served while injured. The fact that he had surgery before the agreement was reached gave him more of a buffer than the NFL knew about, expanding the window during which the suspension could be fully served before the end of the 2026 season without Nacua missing time due to the suspension. Which would still allow Nacua to have this issue behind him before the 2027 offseason, when he signs a new contract with the Rams, has the franchise tag applied, or becomes a free agent.

Of course, Nacua now needs to tread lightly. The league has made it clear that "any further violation of the Personal Conduct Policy, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, will subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the League." To the extent that the league isn't thrilled by the perception/reality that it allowed Nacua to serve his suspension at a time when he otherwise could not play, the league could be ready to pounce on any opportunity to impose a longer suspension that would apply when Nacua is healthy again.

item.title: Philadelphia mayor wants the Eagles to play in a dome
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Eagles will become an indoor team if the mayor of Philadelphia gets her way.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles will become an indoor team if the mayor of Philadelphia gets her way.

“I want a dome,” Mayor Charelle L. Parker said on 93.3 WMMR, via the Philadelphia Inquirer. “Don’t you tell. This is a secret between us. I just saw a rendering of this beautiful dome that they’re talking about for the Bears.”

Moving into a dome would change the character of late-season and playoff games in Philadelphia, which are often affected by snow, wind and cold. Plenty of fans won't like it. But politicians and NFL owners often prefer stadiums with roofs because they bring in lucrative events, indoor sports, concerts, conventions and trade shows.

The Eagles told season ticket holders last year that they are looking at either renovations to Lincoln Financial Field or a new stadium. Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie has committed only to staying in "the region," not in the city of Philadelphia, but both Parker and Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro have said they want the Eagles to remain in the city.

The Eagles' lease at Lincoln Financial Field runs through the 2032 season.

item.title: Jaguars saw something in Liam Coen that other teams didn't
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Jaguars identified Coen as their No. 1 candidate and re-shaped their front office to get him, at a time when other teams weren't even interviewing him.
item.content:encoded:
In a season and a half with the Jaguars, Liam Coen has established himself as one of the best coaches in the NFL. Last year, Coen took over a team that had gone 4-13 the year before and improved their record to 13-4 — the best record ever for a first-year coach taking over a team that had won four or fewer games the year before. This year Coen is showing that last year was no fluke, with the Jaguars at 7-2 with an NFL-best point differential of +125.

Coen's great success should have other teams that hired new head coaches in 2025 asking themselves: What did we miss? Because the Jaguars were so high on Coen that he was their No. 1 target and they were willing to do whatever it took to get him, while no other team even bothered to give Coen an interview.

During the 2025 NFL coaching search, we tracked dozens of reports of head coaching interviews and requests among the seven teams that had vacancies. The Jaguars were the only team that so much as asked Coen to interview.

This week there's been some media scrutiny on the Jets, who hired Aaron Glenn without considering Coen as a candidate. Glenn is 5-22; Coen is 20-6. But it's unfair to single out the Jets for failing to interview Coen, because no team other than the Jaguars did, either.

The 41-year-old Coen had a résumé that should have made him a good candidate. NFL teams area always on the lookout for coaches who can nurture a franchise quarterback and run an innovative offense. Coen played quarterback at UMass and coached quarterbacks in college before getting hired by Sean McVay to work on the Rams' staff, eventually became the Rams' offensive coordinator under McVay, and had been a successful playcaller as offensive coordinator for the Buccaneers, as well as at Kentucky. With that background, it's surprising that only the Jaguars wanted him.

And the Jaguars really wanted him, to the point that they were willing to do whatever it took to hire him. Coen initially turned the Jaguars down and agreed to a contract extension to stay with the Buccaneers, but Jaguars owner Shad Khan wouldn't take no for an answer. When Coen said he was concerned about the direction of the Jaguars' front office, Khan fired General Manager Trent Baalke and agreed to reshape the front office in a way that Coen would approve of if Coen would take the job. Coen was persuaded to take the Jaguars job, and the Jaguars later hired James Gladstone, who had worked with Coen on the Rams, as GM.

The result has been the Jaguars going from one of the worst teams in the NFL to one of the best. Coen's success in Jacksonville has justified the faith Khan had in him. And raises questions about the total lack of interest from the rest of the league.

item.title: Bud Dupree requests release from Chargers, who haven't granted it
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As the season continues to unfold — and as the trade deadline fades into the rear-view mirror — unhappy players have only one option: To request a release.
item.content:encoded:
As the season continues to unfold — and as the trade deadline fades into the rear-view mirror — unhappy players have only one option: To request a release.

Via Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, Chargers linebacker Bud Dupree has done that. The Chargers, however, have not granted the request.

Dupree, per Fowler, also requested his release before the season.

It's unknown whether the Chargers tried to trade him. His playing time has systematically dropped this year. He had no defensive snaps in two straight games before he was a healthy scratch in the Week 10 Monday night game against the Ravens.

That move came three days after Dupree had some pointed comments for the front office.

"Don’t ask hard questions to us; ask hard questions to them,” Dupree said. “Ask the hard questions. Everybody pull they cameras out and go upstairs and ask questions to them. Everybody. Walk upstairs and ask them."

Dupree is under contract, so there's nothing he can do to force his way out. Still, the situation underscores the one-way nature of these deals.

The team can cut the player whenever it wants. The player can't get out unless the team is willing to let him go.

item.title: Puka Nacua will undergo knee surgery and likely miss the rest of the season
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Sean McVay says Nacua will miss "a couple months."
item.content:encoded:
With the football-following world still processing the fact that Rams receiver Puka Nacua will be able to serve a three-game suspension while on injured reserve (and missing at least four games), Nacua apparently will miss more than the minimum.

Via Nate Atkins of The Athletic, coach Sean McVay said Friday that Nacua will undergo surgery to repair a torn MCL and likely will miss the rest of the season.

Per McVay, Nacua is out "a couple months."

In two months exactly, the divisional round will be looming. The Rams will have to get to the playoffs — and past the divisional round — without him.

Then, the question will be whether he's ready for the round of eight. And so on, for as long as the Rams survive.

Meanwhile, Rams receiver Davante Adams remains on IR with a hamstring injury.

This week, the Rams are on a bye. They host the Packers on Wednesday night, followed by games against the Chiefs, 49ers, Cowboys, Seahawks, Buccaneers, and Seahawks.

item.title: Nicolas Cage on his John Madden misfire: "I'm not Frank Caliendo"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: This whole thing is antithetical to my identity.
item.content:encoded:
This whole thing is antithetical to my identity.

That's the one line that resonates most strongly in the new Madden movie. Because it's exactly what John Madden would say if he saw it.

It's bad. It's very bad. Anyone who says it's good has no taste and/or an agenda that involves the strategic application of lips to asses.

The biggest problem is Nicolas Cage as John Madden. Anyone who vividly remembers the unique charisma of John Madden knows instantly that nothing about Cage's portrayal reflects the true nature, spirit, and demeanor of one of the most important and impactful figures in the entire history of the sport of football.

Cage, who seems to realize that his portrayal missed not only the bull's-eye but also the entire wall on which the dart board was mounted, has defended the outcome by peering down his nose at the sports world.

“He was not on my radar," Cage said of Madden, via Kirsten Chuba of the Hollywood Reporter. "I was growing up watching black-and-white Orson Welles movies and Fellini movies and Bruce Lee. I wasn’t interested in team sports whatsoever."

And it shows.

"I’m someone that likes to stay out of his comfort zone and take a risk, I said yes, because that would be a transformation,” Cage explained regarding the decision to attempt to play the towering, iconic figure. “It would be something where I might learn a few things, taking on this character who is really nothing like me.”

The audience has learned that Cage's interpretation is nothing like Madden.

“That’s what acting’s about," Cage said. "I’m not an impressionist, I’m not Frank Caliendo. I lean more towards being a surrealist, meaning I like to get a concept of a personality and then dig deep and see what I can locate emotionally with my imagination and my psyche and filter it through the cadence and the appearance, within reason, of John Madden. I’m trying to give you an evocation, more or less, or an interpretation.”

The problem was it wasn't even "within reason." It was without reason. And the entire film was beyond unreasonable.

And I like Nicolas Cage. He was brilliant in Moonstruck. He won an Oscar for Leaving Las Vegas. And The Family Man remains a highly underrated holiday film.

Still, to quote another holiday film, "They can't all be winners." Cage's role in Madden as John Madden is not.

I only met John Madden once. I watched him on TV for decades. I've heard plenty of stories about him from people who worked with him at NBC. And I'm confident that he would be livid about this film.

"That's not me," he'd say. "Not even close."

Or, perhaps, "This whole thing is antithetical to my identity."

item.title: Carson Beck listed as questionable, but Josh Johnson is expected to start
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Josh Johnson is expected to start Sunday's game against the Chiefs, but the Cardinals have not ruled out Carson Beck.
item.content:encoded:
Josh Johnson is expected to start Sunday's game against the Chiefs, but the Cardinals have not ruled out Carson Beck.

The team lists Beck as questionable with back spasms.

Johnson would become the fourth starting quarterback for the Cardinals this season, following Jacoby Brissett, Gardner Minshew and Beck.

Beck was expected to start the rest of the season after making his first start last Sunday. Beck, though, was listed as limited on Thursday's practice report, and he did not practice Friday.

Beck was sidelined with back spasms earlier this season, too.

The Cardinals ruled out offensive guard Jon Gaines II, who will miss another game with an ankle injury. He returned to practice on Wednesday but did not participate the rest of the week.

Defensive lineman Zach Carter also won't play. He remains on injured reserve, in his 21-day practice window, as he works his way back from a knee injury.

item.title: Brock Bowers doesn't know whether he will play Sunday
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
item.content:encoded:
Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos. Even Bowers, who has quad and ankle injuries, doesn't know if he will play.

"We’ll see," he said, via Ryan McFadden of ESPN.

Bowers didn't practice Wednesday but was limited Thursday and Friday. He said he was "feeling all right," but can't say whether he will play.

"I don't know. We still have some conversations to have," Bowers said.

Bowers injured his right ankle on the opening drive of the Raiders' 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. He tried to play through it before leaving for good.

Bowers played 11 snaps, and he caught two passes for 18 yards.

"I really wanted to play, so I was just doing everything I could to get back out there, like just trying a new tape job and stuff," Bowers said. "Felt it each time I went back out there. It was tough."

Bowers has 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns this season.

item.title: Colts officially place Daniel Jones on waivers
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Daniel Jones is officially on the waiver wire.
item.content:encoded:
Daniel Jones is officially on the waiver wire.

The NFL transaction report has gone out this afternoon, and Jones appears as a waiver from the Colts. After the trade deadline, every player who gets released by his team has to go on waivers before he becomes a free agent.

That means any team that wants Jones on his current contract can claim him, but that is extraordinarily unlikely to happen. As the waiver transaction notes, Jones is a vested veteran with a fully guaranteed salary for the rest of this season. No team is going to want to claim that salary.

Once he clears waivers, however, he'll be an unrestricted free agent, free to sign with any team, and it won't be surprising if some team wants to add him for veteran depth. Jones has been terrible this season, but he's been a competent starter at times in his career, and a team that wants an experienced backup may be interested in signing him for a minimal salary.

Jones was also waived almost exactly two years ago, on November 22, 2024. He cleared waivers and signed with the Vikings' practice squad before signing with the Colts after that season.

item.title: NFL will consider requiring minimum-night stays for international games
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After the 49ers and the Rams took dramatically different approaches to their arrival in Melbourne for the first-ever Australia game, we raised the question of whether the league should require teams to get there early enough to advance the goal of promoting American football to international audiences.
item.content:encoded:
After the 49ers and the Rams took dramatically different approaches to their arrival in Melbourne for the first-ever Australia game, we raised the question of whether the league should require teams to get there early enough to advance the goal of promoting American football to international audiences.

That could be coming.

Via The Athletic, the NFL will consider adopting a minimum-night stay for teams playing internationally.

“Currently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club,” NFL executive V.P. of club business, major events, and international Peter O’Reilly told The Athletic. “It is something that we’ll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It’s something we’ll look at.”

The league already does it for the Super Bowl, mandating a full-week experience that includes multiple press conferences, the annual "Opening Night" media extravaganza, and practicing at designated facilities.

“Having access to players and that type of experience when they’re in the market does have a lasting impact,” O’Reilly said. “That’s a factor when you start to think about encouraging or potentially looking at a policy where you’d want a club in the market for more than the day before.”

Beyond impacting strategic considerations, it would add to the total expense. The money would be worth it, if it further enhances the league's overall reason for going global.

item.title: Saints officially waive S Justin Reid
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Safety Justin Reid already penned his good-bye missive to the Saints, but his departure did not become official until 4 p.m.
item.content:encoded:
Safety Justin Reid already penned his good-bye missive to the Saints, but his departure did not become official until 4 p.m. ET.

The Saints waived Reid on Friday, with the move made official on the NFL's personnel notice.

Reid asked for his release this week, and the Saints have granted it.

“In life and sports, things don’t always go the way you planned or hoped they would,” Reid wrote on social media. “Unfortunately, this is one of those moments. But that doesn’t change the love and respect I have for this organization or city. I truly want to see this team and this city thrive. No one deserves it more than New Orleans and the Saints.”

He will go through waivers, with the NFL announcing at 4 p.m. ET on Monday whether he clears. If no team claims him, Reid will become a free agent.

Reid joined the Saints as a free agent in 2025, and he started all 24 games he played for the team. He had 118 tackles, an interception and a half-sack.

item.title: Fan dies after falling during a fight at 49ers-Cowboys game
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: A man who attended Sunday's game between the 49ers and Cowboys has died due to injuries sustained in a fight during the game.
item.content:encoded:
A man who attended Sunday's game between the 49ers and Cowboys has died due to injuries sustained in a fight during the game.

Via The Independent, 36-year-old Marco Narro was involved in an altercation with another fan near kickoff to the game. During the fight, Narro fell. After the incident, Narro stayed and watched the game.

During the game, he started to complain about pain. He and a friend sought attention from paramedics after the game. Narro was then transported to a local hospital.

On Wednesday, Narro died. An autopsy is pending.

The Arlington Police Department has opened a formal investigation. The prevalence of security cameras at AT&T Stadium should be useful when it comes to reconstructing the events.

The situation underscores one of the basic risks of engaging in fights at sporting events. It doesn't take much to suffer, or to inflict, a very serious injury.

item.title: Giants are Colts' next opponent, and John Harbaugh is taken aback by Daniel Jones news
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Giants coach John Harbaugh is preparing right now for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
Giants coach John Harbaugh is preparing right now for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. But a week later, he'll be coaching against the Colts. And he was taken by surprise today when he found out that the Colts have cut quarterback Daniel Jones.

Harbaugh was visibly surprised at his press conference today when a reporter informed him that Jones has been released, and he said when asked about the work his advance scouts are doing on the Colts that it will certainly change things.

"Yeah, probably pretty dramatically," Harbaugh said. "I mean, wow. I don't want to get ahead of ourselves here. You just hit me with that."

Harbaugh said the Giants will still watch plenty of tape of the Colts' offense this season, but they'll also have to watch tape of Anthony Richardson.

"The offense will be the offense they run, but it will be centered around the quarterback, for sure," Harbaugh said. "And they're probably different styles to some degree, so we'll have to look at that when the time comes. We have people doing that this week. They'll have to make a left turn, obviously. Thanks for the info."

Richardson is a great athlete with a big arm, and the Colts loved him coming out of Florida, and he'll now have until the end of the season to show whether he can in any way resemble the quarterback the Colts thought they were getting when they took him fourth overall in the 2023 NFL draft. Harbaugh's Giants will be the first defense Richardson faces for his first meaningful playing time in two years.
